brief: Seen from a low angle, a gloved hand lifts a whole frozen disc of ice out of a steel dog bowl and holds it up against a pale winter sky. Overhead, a crisp circular halo rings the sun, with faint inner russet and outer lavender. The sky is a soft spray gradation of milky cerulean. The ice disc is hyperreal: trapped bubbles, a fur strand, radiating fracture feathers and frost rime. These are drawn in fine pencil with white-reserved highlights. The ice and the halo circle rhyme as two rings.

A garden hose lies in sinuous whiplash curves across a sunlit lawn, its nozzle throwing a looping arc of water. The spray is drawn as an elegant sweep of ribbon-like loops ending in hyperreal droplets, each with a refracted miniature of the sky. The hose has cracked green vinyl, a brass coupling and a dusty sheen. A confident brown-ink contour of variable weight sets the Art Nouveau rhythm. Watercolour fills it in olive, sage, mustard and pale celadon. The lawn is done in fine individual grass blades, and the picture is cropped as a tall decorative panel.

A rose-pink sandstone lattice screen fills the frame frontally, carved in interlocking hexagonal star openings. Each stone edge shows chisel tooling, pitting and dusty weathering. In one opening, a rose-ringed parakeet grips the stone. Its feathers are rendered barb by barb in viridian, lime and turquoise watercolour, with a coral beak and an inky eye-ring. Through the other openings, a hazy ochre courtyard dissolves into soft washes. The warm, even light makes the screen's depth read through layered shadow glazes rather than strong contrast.

A close-up of a child's face puffing out its cheeks at birthday candles, rendered in exacting detail: the frosting gloss, wax drips, flame halos and sparkling saliva. Horizontal bands of the image are torn and shoved sideways, with a ragged noise strip rolling through the lower third. Chroma bleeds into magenta and cyan fringes along every edge. The medium is layered spray for the soft video glow, with marker bars for the displaced slices. The palette is washed-out tungsten orange, peach and teal. It feels like a home recording degrading.

A top-down view of a torn paper bag of trail mix scattered across a polished terrazzo floor. Real cashews, raisins, sunflower seeds and candy-coated chocolates echo the floor's own chips of marble, so the eye struggles to tell aggregate from snack. The floor is built from flat marker chips of terracotta, slate grey, cream and verdigris set in a speckled putty ground. The foods are layered watercolour with crisp pen highlights and pinpoint specular glints. The composition is all-over and edge-to-edge, with no centre. A faint ceiling reflection streaks diagonally across the polished surface.

A faded indigo work apron hangs from an iron hook on a whitewashed plank wall, filling the frame. Its worn patches are reinforced with dense white running stitches in persimmon-flower and wave patterns. The cloth is built from deep Prussian and slate-blue watercolour washes, mottled where the dye has rubbed thin at the pocket edges. Every stitch is a separate short pen dash with a slight thread twist and a tiny shadow. A chalk smudge, a brass rivet and a loose hanging thread add realism. Raking light from a window catches the ridges of the quilting.

A full English breakfast sculpted entirely in plasticine, painted with obsessive photographic fidelity. The egg yolk has a fingerprint whorl, the bacon is rolled into streaky stripes, the beans are lumpy pellets and the toast is scored with modelling-tool marks. Every surface shows a satin clay sheen, smeared colour seams and tiny dust specks. Hard tabletop lamps cast doubled shadows across a chunky checked tablecloth. The medium is opaque layered watercolour with crisp pencil detailing, in saturated toy hues: cadmium yellow, salmon, tomato and bread tan.

A carved birch ladle tips forward, spilling lingonberries across a gleaming golden-ochre lacquer tray. The tray's own painted curling grass motifs in cinnabar and black flow around the real fruit. Each berry is a glossy wet watercolour sphere in crimson and vermilion, with a sharp white window highlight and a tiny dark calyx. Warm reflected gold flushes the undersides of the berries. Fine pen tendrils and droplet dots weave between them, so the decoration and the harvest read as one continuous flourish. The palette is gold, scarlet and lamp black only.

A poster-like vertical. A ranger's weathered hands hold heavy binoculars, and the twin lenses reflect a sunset canyon in miniature. The setting is reduced to stacked flat bands of burnt sienna, teal, mustard and cream, laid with layered spray and opaque marker. The binoculars themselves are hyperreal: worn black leatherette, scuffed brass, a frayed strap, and a coated lens flare in amber and violet. A bold horizon line cuts behind the hands. There are no letters, only the poster's confident simplification colliding with forensic surface detail.

A wrought-iron fire escape spirals down at impossible, steeply canted angles, with shadows painted as hard black wedges across a cracked plaster wall. A single abandoned patent-leather shoe sits on one step. The medium is compressed charcoal mass with erased white-chalk highlights, all in grey, soot and bone. The distortion is theatrical, but the textures are exact: flaking rust scale, rivet heads, crazed leather, mortar grit. The light comes from one unseen low source and throws jagged diagonal stripes. The mood is menacing and stagey.

A farmhouse wall painted in a horizontal frieze of flat stylised kurbits gourds in red-orange, leaf green and cobalt, outlined in confident black, on a weathered blue-grey plank ground. Pinned over this decoration, a pair of wet knitted wool mittens hangs on a string. They are hyperreal, with felted stitches, a darn, steam faintly rising and drip stains darkening the paint below. The flat folk painting is laid in marker and gouache-like fills. The mittens are dense pencil and watercolour. The composition is a frontal band.

A black-and-tan dog mid-shake, its head a blur of flung ears and jowls. Huge sweeping arcs of thrown water are slashed across the sheet in broad charcoal and dragged marker strokes, gestural and violent. The water spray is spattered in dark accents. At the dead centre, one eye and wet nose are rendered with total hyperreal precision: the moist nostril crease, the reflected window in the cornea, droplets clinging to whiskers. The palette is charcoal, raw umber and cold grey, with a single burst of sky-blue in the spray.

A hyperreal overhead study of a tightened calfskin drumhead scattered with coarse sea salt. The grains have been shaken into nodal rings, petals and radiating spokes by a held tone. The whole sheet is warm sepia and bone, built from patient graphite stipple and fine pen dotting. Each crystal is a tiny faceted cube with a pinpoint highlight and a hairline shadow. Bare skin between the figures shows mottled translucency, fine veins and a tacked rim of tarnished brass lugs cropped at the corners. The light is raking and low from one side, so every salt ridge throws a long grain of shade. The feeling is of something stilled mid-hum.

A sprite sheet laid out as a rigid grid of equal cells on flat chroma-magenta. Each cell holds the same scuffed canvas sneaker toe, and from cell to cell a frayed white shoelace advances through tying a bow, frame by frame. Each frame is rendered hyperreal with layered alcohol marker and fine-liner: aglet plastic shine, lace weave and grubby eyelet rims. Thin cyan registration ticks and tiny frame labels sit in the gutters. The repetition reads as animation. The gestalt is a technical, catalogue-like grid full of micro-variation.

Three marzipan piglets huddle on a crinkled glassine bonbon cup, seen at tabletop height. Draw them in densely burnished coloured pencil on toned buff paper: shell pink, almond cream and a blush of carmine at the snouts. The matte, slightly greasy paste shows thumbprint dimples and toothpick-pricked nostrils. Faint sprayed icing-sugar dust settles in the creases. The background is soft, unfocused pistachio green. Light is warm and diffuse with no hard shadows. Every grain of sugar is visible. The mood is cloying and sweet, yet uncanny in its exactness.

A crumpled school milk carton with a bent striped straw is rendered hyperreal in a single violet ditto-machine ink on pulpy off-white paper. Everything is one hue, from deep methyl violet in the shadows to faint lilac in the highlights. Waxy cardboard creases, a printed cow logo and a drip of milk are all drawn in fine pen and soft marker. The edges fade and ghost unevenly as if the stencil is tiring. There are faint offset smudges and a duplicated echo line at one side. The feel is nostalgic and institutional, yet strangely precise.

A window-washer's gondola hangs against a modernist glass curtain wall, seen from a level adjacent floor. The rigid grid of mullions slices the scene. Each pane reflects a slightly misaligned fragment of sky, a crane and a neighbouring tower, warped by subtle glass bowing. Render it in cool alcohol markers and ruled fine-liner: steel blue, smoky teal and silver grey. Squeegee streaks and soap film stand out on a few panes. The worker's orange harness is the only warm accent. The composition is a fractured, architectural mosaic with vertiginous calm.

An overhead view of a wet blue-grey slate roof just after hail. Dozens of hailstones of varied sizes lie scattered across overlapping tiles, and a few are split open to show onion-ring frozen strata. Render it in graphite and white charcoal on mid-grey paper. Cloudy ice cores are smudged soft, clear outer shells are cut with crisp eraser-white highlights, and meltwater beads form under each stone. The slates show fine cleavage lines and lichen spots. The palette is cold, near-monochrome slate, pewter and frost white. The scattered rhythm feels sudden, percussive and freezing.

A lacquered bento box is half-wrapped in crumpled chiyogami paper, cropped tight and seen from slightly above. The printed pattern of vermilion cranes, plum blossoms and gold-flecked waves bends and breaks over every crease. The fidelity is total: the paper's fibrous edges, a soft sheen on each fold ridge, and shadowed valleys in indigo-grey. Build it from opaque, gouache-like watercolour layers with fine pen for the printed motifs. Small metallic gold specks catch the light. The palette is saturated persimmon, indigo, leaf green and cream. It feels festive and densely ornamented.

A weathered mountaineer's face is seen in close three-quarter view. Frost clings to the stubble and eyelashes, and chapped lips show sunburn. One side is struck by rose-coral alpenglow, the other sinks into cobalt and violet shadow. Work it in soft chalky pastel mass and fine coloured pencil on deep prussian-blue paper, letting the paper serve as the cold midtones. Ice crystals are tiny opaque white points. A blurred pink ridge glows behind him. The mood is exhausted, elated and fleeting, a summit moment held still.
